project.name: Gimle Example: greeter-provider
project.description: A real, deployable Gimle module exercising the platform's actual capabilities: a lifecycle hook that registers a fabric service on startup, and liveness/readiness probes the worker's probe loop calls directly -- unlike hello-module (deliberately minimal, no hooks/probes at all), this bundles genuine ModuleLifecycleHooks/probe implementations inside its own jar, the real deploy shape (as opposed to every dynamically-loaded test fixture elsewhere in this codebase, which leaves its hooks class outside the fixture jar on the test's own classpath). com.gimle.module and org.slf4j are declared `requires static`, not `requires`, because the worker JVM's platform layer is boot-only today (gimle-api doesn't exist yet to be a real platform module -- see PlatformLayer/ModuleLayerFactory in gimle-module): a plain `requires` would fail Configuration resolution outright. ModuleLayerFactory grants this module's layer readability to the parent (unnamed) module at construction time, which is what actually makes the bundled classes resolve against the platform's real types at runtime.
